newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening higher after retail data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening higher after retail data.

text.p: Wall Street was expected to edge higher on Thursday after the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. May retail sales data.
The Commerce Department reported a 0.1 percent decline in May retail sales. Excluding the automobile component, the sales also slipped 0.1 percent.
Wall Street economists had expected an increase of 0.4 percent for the month.
Analysts said the bond market and the futures index rallied higher on the retail numbers, signalling a strong opening for equities.
"The bonds are way up and the futures are up. It looks like we are going to have another rip-roaring day," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

But Philip Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division, said the tame retail data may not affect stocks in the face of possible volatility in two leading technology stocks, Intel Corp and International Business Machines Corp.
